dedupe_keys.name: severe wind hazard assessment for queensland tropical cyclone scenario data geoscience australia

description: The Severe Wind Hazard Assessment for Queensland was a project between Geoscience Australia and Queensland Fire and Emergency Services to understand the potential impacts of tropical cyclones on population centres and critical infrastructure, prompted by lessons from Severe Tropical Cyclone Debbie in 2017. Scenarios were selected from the synthetic event catalogue of the 2018 Tropical Cyclone Hazard Assessment with the fire and emergency service and local governments; for each location a Category 3 and a Category 5 cyclone on tracks favourable for impact analysis were modelled, with regional historical analogues to relate outputs to lived events. Scenario data are downloadable as ZIP files for Cairns, Gladstone, Gold Coast, Kowanyama, Mackay, Mornington Island, Pormpuraaw and Townsville (from about 125 MB to 3 GB each), with a scenario data description document. Geoscience Australia published it in December 2022; the metadata states copyright of the Commonwealth of Australia and no separate licence. Caveats: the provider stresses that each real cyclone will differ, the events are synthetic, and the scenarios cover eight communities. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response planning for wind impacts on buildings and infrastructure and testing emergency service capability; a related record is IBTrACS.
